read.sections.0.heading.source: Remembering is a choice made in the present
read.sections.0.heading.back: Remembering is a choice made in the present

read.sections.0.text.source:
A monument is made at a particular time to remember something. Its subject may belong to a much earlier period. So studying it involves two historical questions. What is being remembered? And why did later people choose to remember it in this form? The artist, the people who commissioned it, its place and its audience all shape that public account.

In the 1880s, the French town of Calais commissioned a monument from Auguste Rodin. It would commemorate, or publicly remember, citizens linked with the Hundred Years' War. Rodin drew on the medieval writer Jean Froissart's account of the siege of 1347. In that account, six leading citizens offered themselves to England's King Edward III in exchange for the town's protection. Rodin's sculpture shows them setting out, when their fate was uncertain. It is a nineteenth-century interpretation of a medieval story, not an eyewitness record.
read.sections.0.text.back:
A monument is made at a particular time to remember something. Its subject may belong to a much earlier period. So studying it involves two historical questions. What is being remembered? And why did later people choose to remember it in this form? The artist, the people who commissioned it, its place and its audience all shape that public account.

In the 1880s, the town of Calais in France commissioned a monument from Auguste Rodin. The monument would commemorate, that is, remember openly, citizens connected with the Hundred Years' War. Rodin used the account of the Middle Ages writer Jean Froissart about the siege in 1347. In that account, six leading citizens gave themselves up to King Edward III of England in exchange for the town's protection. Rodin's sculpture shows them as they start to walk away, when their fate was not yet certain. This sculpture is a 19th-century interpretation of a story from the Middle Ages, not an eyewitness record.

read.sections.0.simpler.source:
A monument helps people remember. It may be about a much earlier time. So we ask two questions. What is remembered? And why did later people remember it this way? The artist, the people who paid, the place and the viewers all matter.

In the 1880s, the town of Calais in France asked Rodin for a monument. It would commemorate some of its people from a long war. To commemorate means to remember in public. Rodin used a story by Jean Froissart, a writer from the Middle Ages. In 1347, an army surrounded Calais. Six leading men offered themselves to England's king, Edward III. In return, he would keep the town safe. Rodin shows the men as they leave, not knowing what will happen. He made it more than 500 years later.
read.sections.0.simpler.back:
A monument helps people remember something. A monument may be about a much earlier time. So we ask two questions. What is remembered? And why did later people remember it in this way? The artist, the people who paid, the place and the viewers all matter.

In the 1880s, the town of Calais in France asked Rodin to make a monument. The monument would commemorate some of its people from a long war. To commemorate means to remember in front of many people. Rodin used a story by Jean Froissart, a writer from the Middle Ages. In 1347, an army surrounded Calais. Six leading men gave themselves up to England's king, Edward III. In return, the king would keep the town safe. Rodin shows the men as they leave, not knowing what will happen. He made it more than 500 years later.

read.sections.1.text.source:
The group has six figures, each with a different gesture and expression. Rodin placed them all on one level instead of raising one above the others. Plain clothes and vulnerable poses make the monument very different from a statue of a victorious ruler on horseback. Here, civic courage, the courage of a town's citizens, appears as people facing a hard choice together. Each one responds in his own way.

The town council had first planned a monument to Eustache de Saint-Pierre, the best-known citizen in the group. By including all six, Rodin shifted attention toward a shared action. This was a choice about public memory as well as composition. Deciding whom to show helped define the story the town would remember in public.

A separate figure, Jean d'Aire, helps us study those decisions. The National Gallery of Art's version shows a clothed man standing firmly and holding a large key. His posture and hands give the figure weight. A whole group and a single study offer different views of the same larger project. Their size and the way they are displayed also affect how an audience meets them.
read.sections.1.text.back:
The group has six figures, each with a different gesture and facial expression. Rodin placed them all on one level, instead of raising one above the others. Plain clothes and weak body poses make this monument very different from a statue of a victorious ruler riding a horse. Here, civic courage, that is, the courage of the people of a town, appears as people facing a hard choice together. Each person responds in his own way.

The town council at first planned a monument to Eustache de Saint-Pierre, the best-known citizen in the group. By including all six, Rodin shifted attention to a shared action. This was a choice about public memory as well as about composition. Deciding whom to show helped define the story the town would remember openly.

A separate figure, Jean d'Aire, helps us study those decisions. The National Gallery of Art's version shows a clothed man standing firmly and holding a large key. His body pose and hands give the figure a sense of weight. One complete group and one single study give different views of the same big project. Their size and the way the work is displayed also affect how the audience meets it.
read.sections.1.text.note: "civic" is "sivik", the Malaysian school word (as in "Sivik"); "vulnerable" is given as "lemah" (weak, exposed). Reviewer to check both. "project" here is Rodin's monument, not Thinkerwell.

read.sections.1.simpler.source:
The monument has six men. Each one moves and looks in a different way. Rodin put them all on one level. They wear plain clothes. Their poses look weak, not proud. They are not like a king on a horse. It shows civic courage. Civic means about a town and its people. Here, courage means facing a hard choice together. But each man reacts in his own way.

At first, the town wanted a monument to one man, Eustache de Saint-Pierre. He was the best known of the six. Rodin showed all six instead. So the monument is about a shared act. Choosing whom to show shaped the story the town remembers.

Rodin also made a single figure, Jean d'Aire. A man stands firmly and holds a large key. His body and hands look strong. Their size and how they are shown change how we see them.
read.sections.1.simpler.back:
The monument has six men. Each one moves and looks in a different way. Rodin put them all on one level. They wear plain clothes. Their body poses look weak, not proud. They are not like a king on a horse. This monument shows civic courage. Civic means about a town and its people. Here, being brave means facing a hard choice together. But each man reacts in his own way.

At first, the town wanted a monument to one man only, Eustache de Saint-Pierre. He was the best known of the six. Rodin showed all six. So the monument is about a shared action. Choosing whom to show shaped the story the town remembers.

Rodin also made a single figure, Jean d'Aire. A man stands firmly and holds a large key. His body and hands look strong. The size of the figures and how they are displayed change how we see them.

read.sections.2.heading.source: An artist's travels and a bronze's dates
read.sections.2.heading.back: An artist's travels and a bronze's dates

read.sections.2.text.source:
Rodin's career also crossed borders. He grew up in a working-class district of Paris and trained in the decorative arts. After the Franco-Prussian War of 1870–71 disrupted work, he continued his career in Belgium. A later journey to Italy deepened his interest in Michelangelo's sculpture. Calling Rodin a French artist names an important connection. But his skills developed through particular schools, jobs and travel. Artistic culture was shaped by movement as well as by local institutions.

Dates need particular care with sculpture. A model can be made first, and a bronze cast, an object formed in a mould, can be produced much later. The Met's group was modelled in 1884–95 but cast in 1985. The National Gallery of Art's smaller Jean d'Aire was modelled in 1884–89 and probably cast in 1895. Neither is a bronze made at the time of the medieval event, and each museum object is a separate cast.
read.sections.2.text.back:
Rodin's career also crossed borders. He grew up in a working-class area of Paris and was trained in decorative arts. After the Franco-Prussian War of 1870–71 disrupted work, he continued his career in Belgium. A later journey to Italy deepened his interest in Michelangelo's sculpture. Calling Rodin a French artist names an important connection. But his skills developed through particular schools, jobs and journeys. Artistic culture was shaped by movement as well as by local institutions.

Dates need special attention with sculpture. A model can be made first, and a bronze cast, that is, an object formed in a mould, can be produced much later. The Met's group had its model made in 1884–95 but was cast in 1985. The National Gallery of Art's smaller Jean d'Aire had its model made in 1884–89 and was probably cast in 1895. Neither is a bronze made at the time of the Middle Ages event, and each museum object is a separate cast.

read.sections.2.simpler.source:
Rodin's life also crossed borders. He grew up in a part of Paris where working people lived. He learned to make decorations. A war in 1870 and 1871 stopped much of the work, so he worked in Belgium. Later, in Italy, he studied Michelangelo's sculpture. Rodin was French. But his skills came from schools, jobs and travel.

Dates need care with sculpture. First an artist makes a model. Then a bronze cast is made, maybe much later. A cast is made by pouring metal into a mould. The Met's group is from a model made in 1884–95. But it was cast in 1985. The smaller Jean d'Aire is from a model made in 1884–89. It was probably cast in 1895. Neither was made in 1347. Each one is a separate cast.
read.sections.2.simpler.back:

Dates need attention with sculpture. First an artist makes a model. Then a bronze cast is made, maybe much later. A cast is made by pouring metal into a mould. The Met's group comes from a model made in 1884–95. But the group was cast in 1985. The smaller Jean d'Aire comes from a model made in 1884–89. The figure was probably cast in 1895. write.sentenceStarters.2.source: So the monument shows courage as ...

write.example.source: Rodin chose to show six citizens on the same level, in plain clothes. Each one has a different gesture, and none of them stands above the others. The history tells us that the town council first wanted a monument to just one man, Eustache de Saint-Pierre. So the monument shows courage as something people share. Each man faces the same hard choice in his own way.
write.example.back: Rodin chose to show six citizens on the same level, in plain clothes. Each one has a different gesture, and none of them stands higher than the others. Its history tells us that the town council at first wanted a monument to one man only, Eustache de Saint-Pierre. So the monument shows courage as something shared by many people. Each man faces the same hard choice in his own way.

sensitiveNotes.0.source: The siege story turns on six citizens offering their lives to save their town, during a war. Keep the account brief and non-graphic, and don't ask for any reenactment or role-play of the threatened people. The Franco-Prussian War is named only as the reason Rodin moved to Belgium for work.
sensitiveNotes.0.back: This siege story turns on six citizens offering their lives to save their town, during a war. Tell the account briefly and without gruesome detail, and don't ask learners to re-enact or play the roles of the threatened people. The Franco-Prussian War is named only as the reason Rodin moved to Belgium for work.
